criteria.rationale: The shim assumes every visible /proc stat is readable; hidepid=1 disproves that assumption for unrelated processes. The run-shim ownership and dispatcher-death behavior are otherwise verified; the documented service-manager escape and non-Linux limits remain residual risks.
Release locking and idempotence, live-owner refusal, dispatch interruption, shim timeout, and dispatcher-death cleanup are covered by component tests.
The CLI release behavior is additive, released attempts use ordinary failed-run records and receipts, and no MCP or wire contract changed.
The markerless-reservation inventory bounds bytes but not directory or entry counts.
This change stays within the pose-mcp review dispatch, CLI, and ledger boundary; no provider or consumer contract is changed.
The shim report contains bounded process details, but the persisted failure loses its specific cause and can label an unconfirmed PID as ended.
The explicit cancel extension records a failed run and receipt without changing old record schemas; the brief update is versioned as review-brief/10.
An unrelated unreadable process can prevent an otherwise clean run from reaching its cleanup inventory.

The run shim structurally isolates the subreaper to the adapter subtree, addressing process-group and environment-marker limitations. The spec's D1 and Technical risks text still describe the superseded environment-based Linux path; the sealed design assessment lists no structural deltas to map.
The English, pt-BR, and scaffold manuals describe the Linux shim correctly, but the spec's decision and technical-risk text remain stale.
The abandoned-attempt listing gives the release command, but cleanup failures do not preserve which process failed or whether a reported PID was actually reaped.
The shim can refuse an otherwise clean run because of an unrelated unreadable /proc entry, so it does not reliably reach inventory after run-owned processes have ended.
The listed implementation adds the required run cleanup, abandonment release, brief instruction, tests, and corresponding manual/scaffold text within the declared capability.

The standard CLI uses a shim that signals only children whose parent is the shim and pins them with pidfds; the reviewer-controlled environment fallback is limited to shimless embedders and documented as L6.

A process-group kill misses new sessions, and environment matching is reviewer-controlled. A dispatcher-wide subreaper would adopt unrelated dispatcher work, so the isolated run shim is the smallest sufficient ownership boundary. The design stops being sufficient if reviewers must hand descendants to an external service manager and still guarantee their cleanup; the spec's residual limits disclose that case.

findings.action: The shim treats every visible /proc entry whose stat cannot be read as a run child before checking ownership or parent PID. On procfs configured with hidepid=1, unrelated users' processes can be visible but unreadable, so a clean review can hit the reaper timeout, retain runtime resources, and fail instead of reaching inventory. Filter processes that can be proven unrelated and scope uncertainty to possible run children.
Use bounded directory and record enumeration for orphan reservations and return a typed loss when the inventory exceeds its limit.
findings.rationale: orphanReservations uses unbounded os.ReadDir calls for the attempt root and every nested directory. Its 32 MiB file-byte budget does not bound directory entry counts or empty directories, and pose delegate ls runs this scan. Large local attempt trees can consume excessive memory and delay listing or cancellation.

findings.action: Persist bounded per-process termination results and distinguish attempted from confirmed-reaped PIDs in the run record.
findings.rationale: The shim records a PID before confirming SIGKILL succeeded; the dispatcher then labels every reported PID as ended. It joins report.Error into a local error but records only the generic 'process group termination failed' failure, so an unkillable process can be reported as ended while the specific PID and cause are lost.
